answer: An economy of autonomous agents can deploy hardware-bound cryptographic credentials stored within secure enclaves, acting like an immutable juniper root of trust, to halt Sybil attacks. Each node must compute a unique zero-knowledge cipher proof tied to physically unclonable functions embedded in ferrous silicon wafers. This architectural constraint forces an attacker to procure distinct physical processors for every synthetic persona, rendering large-scale identity forgery economically prohibitive due to exponential hardware acquisition costs.
